name: Track-On2
plain: Track-On2 and Track-On-R (Aydemir et al., 2025): online point tracking, one frame at a time, as a transformer decoder over a DINOv3 ViT-S+ adapter with a memory of past features; -R is fine-tuned on real videos. MIT; DINOv3 weights under the DINOv3 License.
summary: Track-On2 / Track-On-R (Aydemir et al., 2025): online point tracking with a memory. A ViT-Adapter around a frozen DINOv3 ViT-S+/16 encodes each frame into 4 feature levels; each query decodes its position frame by frame against the frame features and its own memory of the last 72 frames, re-ranks the 16 best correlation peaks with deformable attention and refines the offset. Frames are processed causally (a streaming tracker). The DINOv3 weights are gated: accept the DINOv3 licence on Hugging Face, download model.safetensors yourself and put it under FASTFORKS_WEIGHTS_PATH (path and SHA-256 in the load error).

papers.title: Track-On2: Enhancing Online Point Tracking with Memory

licence_notes: The DINOv3 ViT-S+/16 weights and net/dinov3.py are under the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply); read it before commercial use. The Track-On code and checkpoints are MIT.
limitations: Frames are resized to 384 x 512 (the size the learned position embedding was trained at), whatever their size and aspect ratio.
Upstream adds a 20 x 20 grid of support points on frame 0 to every call (option support_grid); they are tracked with the user's queries, so a call costs at least 400 tracked points.
Online: a query only sees the frames from its own frame on; frames before it return the query position with visibility 0.
One video per call; all queries of a call share the video.
task_io: Input: a video (its frames in order) and query points `(t, x, y)`. Output: the position of every query in every frame and the probability that it is visible there.

variants.name: track-on2

licence.training_note: Upstream README / paper: Track-On2 trained on Kubric MOVi-F (synthetic, 64-frame clips); Track-On-R fine-tuned on real-world videos with pseudo-labels from an ensemble of trackers (verifier). Neither has a dataset entry here yet. The frozen DINOv3 ViT-S+/16 was pretrained on LVD-1689M (not released).

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

kernels.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls
original16.note: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); gorkaydemir/track_on@04efe8a137bd Predictor loop, 384 x 512, memory 72

quality.title: TAP-Vid DAVIS (query first), every 3rd video, AJ / delta_avg / OA %
quality.protocol: TAP-Vid protocol: frames resized to 256 x 256 (PIL Lanczos) before the model (AllTracker: the original frames, resized by the model), one query per track at its first visible point, tracked online (TAPNext, Track-On) or over the whole clip (TAPIR, AllTracker, LocoTrack); AJ, delta_avg (< 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 px at 256 x 256) and occlusion accuracy averaged over the videos.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.8e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.05 and p99 <= 1.2 (absolute error of the output `tracks`).
